subject: ProofPoint - capacity addendum & pricing holdback coordination
messages:
From: Emily Carter <emily@proofpointlabs.com>
To: connor.obrien@redwood.com, procurement@proofpointlabs.com
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 30 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: add capacity + pricing holdback for Q3

Connor / Procurement team —

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. Quick formal ask so we can get this to procurement and legal here: ProofPoint needs an additional 200 inference nodes (dedicated capacity) to support an expected Q3 spike in batch scoring. We are evaluating a short-term top-up while we finalize our longer-term committed band.

Key asks from our side:
- A change order / addendum to the existing Order Form adding 200 nodes for a 90-day pilot window starting 2025-07-01.
- A 10–15% pricing holdback that we can escrow until functional acceptance (performance and stability over a 7-day acceptance window).
- Clear acceptance criteria and an implementation timeline (we will expect at least 3 days of lead time once signed).
- Proof of SOC 2 controls and a short statement about data retention for cached prompts (we'll include with procurement questionnaire).

Can you send a redlined Order Form and suggested language for the holdback? Procurement here needs a PO + signed change order to move forward. If you can get a doc over by end of day Monday (PT), we will triage with legal and procurement.

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround.

Emily Carter
Director of Cloud Platform
ProofPoint Labs
emily@proofpointlabs.com

Attachment: (none)
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Emily Carter <emily@proofpointlabs.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 30 May 2025 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: add capacity + pricing holdback for Q3

Emily —

Thanks — we can do that. High-level approach we propose so procurement/legal have something concrete to review:

1) Change order (attached redline) that adds a temporary capacity band: +200 nodes, effective 2025-07-01 for 90 days.
2) Pricing holdback: Redwood will invoice 100% at signing, but 12% of the invoice will be held against final acceptance. The holdback is released after the acceptance criteria are met (see proposed checklist in the redline). This is slightly different than escrow language but reduces billing complexity — can adjust if ProofPoint insists on escrow.
3) Acceptance criteria: (a) sustained p95 token latency under 350ms on agreed sample workloads for 7 consecutive days, (b) no more than 1 DR incident impacting the added capacity during the acceptance window. We included a suggested appendix with metrics and a one-paragraph implementation plan.
4) Delivery lead time: we can provision in ~5 business days post-signature for a normal window; if you need a hard 3-day SLA we can mark as expedited with an additional one-time provisioning fee.

I've attached a redlined OrderForm_v3_redline.docx focusing on the new band and the holdback clause. Laura — can you coordinate commercial sign-off? Karthik — can you review the holdback wording for legal comfort and advise if we should switch to escrow?

Next steps: I can upload the final change order to DocuSign once legal and ProofPoint procurement confirm wording.

Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com
Attachment: OrderForm_v3_redline.docx
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: connor.obrien@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 01 Jun 2025 10:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: add capacity + pricing holdback for Q3 (legal suggestions)

On Fri, May 30, 2025 at 11:02 AM Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com> wrote:
> I've attached a redlined OrderForm_v3_redline.docx focusing on the new band and the holdback clause.

Connor / Laura —

Quick legal notes after reviewing the redline: overall this is workable but recommend tightening two items so procurement doesn't come back with costly edits.

1) Holdback mechanism: switch from "invoice reduction" to a "performance holdback" payable on acceptance. Suggested language (replace current paragraph):

"Redwood will invoice the Fee for the Addendum upon execution. An amount equal to 12% of the Fee (the 'Holdback') will be retained by ProofPoint and released to Redwood within 5 Business Days following successful completion of the Acceptance Criteria defined in Appendix A. In the event Acceptance is not achieved within the Acceptance Window through no fault of Redwood, ProofPoint's sole remedy shall be a pro rata refund of the unconsumed Addendum Fees."

This limits scope of remedies and avoids escrow, which procurement hates.

2) Acceptance Criteria scope: define exact test harness and sample dataset IDs rather than vague wording. I put placeholder text in Appendix A; ops will need to confirm dataset IDs with ProofPoint.

3) Termination & rollback: add a short-run rollback clause so we can reclaim capacity without dispute if the addendum is terminated. Simple sentence in the implementation plan should suffice.

4) Data retention/cache line: add a single-sentence commitment on requested TTLs and state that Redwood will not persist customer prompt inputs beyond configured cache TTLs unless otherwise agreed. This should satisfy procurement's questionnaire.

I can produce a tracked-change Word version if you want; otherwise accept my inline edits and I'll greenlight for DocuSign.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Legal (Commercial Contracts)
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

Quoted attachments: OrderForm_v3_redline.docx (reviewed)
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Cc: connor.obrien@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 03 Jun 2025 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: ProofPoint addendum - finalized language and DocuSign link

Emily / Procurement team —

Thanks for the patience. We incorporated Karthik's legal suggestions and tightened the Acceptance Criteria appendix (we used the dataset IDs you shared on the call). The main changes:
- Holdback converted to a "performance holdback" (12% of Addendum Fee) with a 5-business-day release on acceptance.
- Explicit test harness and dataset IDs in Appendix A.
- Rollback procedure added to the implementation plan.
- Single-sentence cache/retention commitment added.

I've attached the finalized change order (ChangeOrder_PP_Addendum_v1.pdf) and opened a DocuSign envelope for signature: https://docusign.example.com/envelope/ABC12345.

Next steps for ProofPoint:
1) Procurement to issue PO referencing Deal ID PP-2025-089. Please attach PO to the DocuSign envelope or reply-all with the PO number.
2) Emily to confirm if you want the expedited 3-day provisioning SLA (there will be a one-time $2,500 provisioning fee).
3) Once signed and PO received, we will provision the additional nodes within 5 business days (or 3 days if expedited).

If you want us to convert the holdback to a true escrow arrangement we can do that, but expect a 7–10 business-day delay while accounts set up the escrow instrument.

Connor will follow up on operational setup once the signature comes through.

Best,

Laura Bennett
Sr. Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
